meta.name: Clean Google Sheets contact data for phone, email, and dates on an hourly schedule

name: Google Sheets Contact Data Cleaner — normalize, validate, review queue, error-safe

parameters.content:
## Setup (5 min)
1. Connect your Google Sheets account in n8n (the three Google Sheets nodes below).
2. In "Read rows" and "Write cleaned rows back", set `documentId` to your spreadsheet and `sheetName` to the tab you want cleaned.
3. In "Flag invalid rows", set `sheetName` to a review tab (e.g. `Needs Review`) — create it once, empty, with the same headers plus `_reason`.
4. In "Normalize phone/email/date", set `PHONE_COL`/`EMAIL_COL`/`DATE_COL` to your actual column headers and `DEFAULT_COUNTRY_PREFIX` to your default dialing code.
5. Activate. Runs hourly.

## What this does
Reads every row of a Google Sheet on a schedule, normalizes messy `phone`/`email`/`date` columns (E.164-ish phone, lowercased/trimmed email, ISO date). Rows with an invalid email are routed to a separate review tab instead of being silently overwritten or dropped. Only rows that actually changed are written back, so it's safe to run continuously without rewriting untouched data or racing other automations on the same sheet.

## Error handling & edge cases
- **Read rows** and both write nodes use `onError: continueRegularOutput`: a failed Google Sheets call becomes a normal item carrying an `error` field instead of throwing and killing the whole run.
- **Read failed?** stops that run cleanly (logged, no partial writes) instead of writing garbage on top of a half-read sheet.
- **Invalid email found?** never overwrites a bad row in place — it copies it to a review tab so a human can fix the source data, and skips writing it back.
- **Write failed?** (both the review-flag write and the main write) is logged separately, so a quota error or a locked sheet doesn't disappear silently — you see exactly which write failed and why on the next run's execution log.
